assumptions: Correction cell rings represent physical source spaces with horizontal floor/ceiling boundaries.
Contacts describe adjacency, not traversability or EnergyPlus surface pairing.
Only explicit openings are represented; absent observations do not establish a solid wall.
Source boundary identity follows cell identity and ring order; topology edits need identity migration.

Plan orientation: x=0 assigned West, x=15 East; the tool's convention places North at y=8 (max Y) and South at y=0 (min Y), cross-checked against the plan's single west-side ground-floor door / east-side corridor windows matching the labelled West/East elevations (no north arrow present on plans).

Uniform wall abstraction: exterior/partition wall thickness not individually modeled; rooms defined on a centerline grid (bays at x=0/5/7.5/10/11.25/15, y=0/3/5/8) derived from the dimension strings, which already reconcile to the 15.0 x 8.0 m envelope.
Floor-to-floor heights (F1=3.0 m, F2=3.6 m, total 6.6 m) taken directly and consistently from all four elevation drawings; F2 elevations use absolute world Z as required (z_floor=3.0).
Window sill/height taken from elevation dimension chains: y=0-row (plan 'North', built facade 'South') and y=8-row windows sill1.0/h1.6m; East/West and all F2 windows sill1.0/h1.8m.

Interior door heights standardized to 2.1 m (not separately dimensioned on plan); the ground-floor South(y=8) entrance and West corridor exterior doors set to 2.4 m based on elevation glazing proportions (literal glazing divisions summed to a full 3.0 m storey height, simplified down to a more conventional tall-door height).
Room F1_S1 (y=5-8 row) small secondary window has no explicit dimension string; its size/position (0.7 m wide, sill 1.8 m) is an inferred placeholder.

Redundant paired door leaves drawn at shared partitions (e.g., F1 N2 and F2 M1/M2 each show two adjacent door arcs to the corridor) are preserved as two separate door objects rather than merged into one, matching the drawing.

No door was modeled between F2 offices O2 and O3 (large 4.38 m gap with no door-leaf marks in the dimension string at that spine wall), even though an automated visual review suggested a possible connecting door there; the dimensioned evidence for the other two office pairs (O1-O2, O3-O4) shows explicit 360+360mm door-leaf markers absent at the O2-O3 wall, so this was treated as a solid wall.

unresolved: No staircase/vertical circulation is drawn on either floor plan; connectivity between F1 and F2 is therefore not represented as a modeled opening (would require fabricating an unevidenced stair location).

Exact wall thicknesses vary in the drawings (240mm exterior, 340mm at corridor partitions, 360mm at some office partitions); the tool's rectangular-cell schema does not carry per-wall thickness, so a single representative centerline grid was used instead of literal face-to-face offsets.
Door swing/open-closed state is not indicated on the drawings for any opening; all doors marked state=unknown.

Minor (<0.3 m) discrepancies exist between the plan's own two independent dimension chains for the corridor width (1500mm vs 1200mm implied by different chains); 2.0 m corridor clear span was adopted as the reconciling value.
